rows.question: What is the sonographic appearance of a seminoma?
What is the sonographic appearance of a testicular cyst?
What is a varicocele and how is it identified on ultrasound?
What is the sonographic appearance of epididymo-orchitis?
What is a hydrocele?
What is a spermatocele?
What is the sonographic appearance of a testicular microlithiasis?
What is the normal epididymis head size?
What is the bell-clapper deformity?
What is the whirlpool sign in testicular torsion?
What is the normal appendix testis appearance?
What is the sonographic appearance of a scrotal hematoma?
What is the sonographic appearance of a Leydig cell tumor?
What is the normal scrotal wall thickness?
What is the difference between CW and PW Doppler?

A 62-year-old male presents with sudden onset of right shoulder pain and weakness after lifting a heavy object. Ultrasound of the shoulder reveals a complete non-retracted tear of the supraspinatus tendon. What key ultrasound finding distinguishes a complete tear from a partial tear?

A 45-year-old tennis player presents with chronic lateral elbow pain. Ultrasound reveals hypoechoic changes and focal thickening at the common extensor tendon origin, with increased Doppler signal. What is the most appropriate diagnosis?

A 38-year-old patient with rheumatoid arthritis presents with right knee pain and swelling. Ultrasound reveals an anechoic collection within the suprapatellar bursa with internal debris and synovial hypertrophy. Which of the following best describes this finding?

A patient presents with numbness and tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers, worse at night. Ultrasound of the wrist reveals flattening of the median nerve at the carpal tunnel inlet and a cross-sectional area of 15 mm². What is the most likely diagnosis?

During a dynamic ultrasound assessment of the shoulder, the sonographer observes impingement of the supraspinatus tendon beneath the acromion during arm abduction. What maneuver is most effective for demonstrating this finding?
